Electricity demand in India increases by an average of six percent each year until 2035.

The article was published on November 19, 2026.
items.title: IEA: India to lead global oil demand growth at 3% annually through 2035

items.summary: After Jensen Huang, Nvidia's founder and former chief executive, resigned amid revelations of extramarital affairs including an allegation involving a suspected Chinese spy, fashion commentators turned to his signature black Tom Ford leather jackets. Fashion journalist Emma Childs argued in The Cut that the garments had 'confessed before he did,' describing them as the outerwear of a man with an active Raya profile and a Harley-Davidson rather than one returning home to family after building the AI revolution. Michael Smith, co-host of the Pair of Kings podcast, added that Huang's jackets were stiff, unbroken in, and showed no creasing, which he read as evidence that 'if a man cannot commit to anything... what makes you think he can commit to you?' The jackets referenced are Tom Ford pieces so coveted that one sold at Sotheby's for nearly $1 million; the auction house called it not only a jacket but also 'the uniform of a first believer.' Huang has repeatedly said his wife and daughter buy the jackets, though Anand Giridharadas wrote in The New York Times that this claim rang hollow to fans who knew where each jacket came from, arguing Huang had 'betrayed the leather-jacket community' by cosplaying as a rebel while masking extraordinary power. Beyond infidelity readings, commentators offered other interpretations of the jackets' meaning. Behavioral psychologist Carolyn Mair told Salon that tech billionaires reject old-money sartorial codes to signal they need not conform because rules do not apply to them at their level; Stanford Law professor Richard Thompson Ford argued in an article by Vanessa Friedman that the jacket signals a down-to-earth rejection of fashionable artifice while still using fashion's power, evoking Marlon Brando and James Dean. Fashion director Vanessa Friedman noted executives like Jeff Bezos and Mark Zuckerberg understand that becoming popular culture rather than merely successful may depend on image, with Alvaro Fernandez-Espina calling it 'a modern armor' appropriating rebellion to certify victory over corporate scrutiny while giving a cool-villain aura fit for a spy movie. Derek Guy told Eugene Rabkin that leather in menswear telegraphs strength and rebellion, which middle-aged techno-oligarchs adopt to balance authority with youthful appeal amid tension between monetary capital and cultural cache. Critics including Thomas Frank lamented businessmen imagining themselves as rebels while becoming ideologists of business, stripping the garment of its original meaning. A viral image of Huang wearing a vintage studded Saint Laurent by Hedi Slimane jacket was later revealed in Vanity Fair to be AI-generated, completing an irony about the prophet of AI watching his signature garment reinvented by that technology. Following his resignation, President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that Tim Cook should replace him while saying he would not mind seeing Huang return; journalist Natasha Lee suggested a cardigan as a uniform 'nobody has ever been caught out by.'
items.title: Jensen Huang's leather jackets read as a confession of infidelity

items.summary:
Shares of Infosys fell as much as 2.49 per cent to ₹1,081.20 in intraday trade on the National Stock Exchange on Thursday, extending a sharp week-long decline even though the company's subsidiary announced a joint venture with Japanese telecom major NTT Docomo. By 12.16 PM the stock was trading at ₹1,081.20, down ₹27.60 from its previous close of ₹1,108.80; it touched an intraday low of ₹1,073.20, not far above its 52-week low of ₹980.40 hit on September 29. The stock opened at ₹1,096.30 and reached a high of ₹1,097.00 before turning sharply lower, with traded volume standing at 54.51 lakh shares worth ₹589.20 crore.

The stock has been a consistent underperformer: it shed 6.10 per cent in the past week, 4.40 per cent over the past month, and is down 33.67 per cent year-to-date, significantly lagging the Nifty 50's 3.02 per cent year-to-date loss. Its 52-week high of ₹1,728.00 was recorded on February 3.

The sell-off comes despite a business development flagged in pre-market notes: Infosys Singapore, a wholly owned subsidiary, will enter a joint venture with NTT Docomo, one of Japan's leading telecommunications companies. The JV, anchored by NTT Docomo and powered by artificial intelligence, will focus on building a virtual economic ecosystem in the metaverse, integrating real businesses with real-world commerce; Infosys has joined NTT Docomo Playspace, Inc. as a strategic partner. SBI Securities described the development as positive for the medium to long term, noting Japan as a key strategic market for Infosys.

However, broader headwinds overrode the stock-specific positive: the Nifty IT index was down 1.50 per cent at the same time, weighed by a strengthening rupee — typically negative for export-dependent software companies — and global concerns about AI-related valuations. Infosys was the worst performer among Nifty IT constituents, declining 2.46 per cent at the index level. The stock's current P/E stands at 14.62, reflecting significant valuation compression from earlier in the year.

The item was published on November 19, 2026.
items.title: Infosys shares fall intraday despite NTT Docomo metaverse JV

items.summary: An upcoming Anthropic initial public offering is expected to generate substantial wealth for its employees, with some early junior and administrative staff potentially earning more than later-joining senior executives. The company disclosed that employee stock options had accumulated approximately $119 billion in paper gains as of September 30, based on a weighted average exercise price of $2.91, of which around $73 billion represented vested gains exercisable immediately. Two model-based estimates have not been independently verified by Reuters: private-markets research firm Sacra suggests roughly 2,800 current and former employees could hold at least $1 million in pretax vested equity if Anthropic achieves a valuation of $1.35 trillion, while the private-share marketplace Hill estimates that 598 non-founder employees could each hold equity worth at least $100 million. The IPO is expected to value Anthropic at approximately $1.5 trillion (£1.1 trillion), potentially placing it among the world's 12 most valuable companies. The disparity between junior and senior staff stems from employee stock options, which let workers buy shares at a predetermined exercise price; early-stage employees typically receive lower prices because valuations were modest then. Options granted through 2023 averaged just $0.52 per share, so the proposed IPO price range of $70–78 represents an extraordinary increase in potential value—for example, an employee holding 10,000 options exercisable at $0.52 could see gross intrinsic value of approximately $774,800 at a $78 IPO price before taxes and exercise costs. Hill CEO Andrew Benson said early employees who started in junior roles should have better financial outcomes than those joining senior right before the IPO. Equity compensation extended beyond engineers: a May 2024 advertisement for an administrative business partner offered a salary of $140,000–190,000 plus equity, and CFO Krishna Rao received 14 million options in 2024 at an exercise price of $1.30, potentially representing approximately $1 billion in gross intrinsic value. Founded in 2021, Anthropic grew from about 940 employees at the end of 2024 to 5,300 by September 2026. The article notes that paper wealth does not automatically become cash: non-founder employees could reportedly sell only 10% of holdings on the first trading day and another 35% after fiscal 2026 earnings, with actual returns depending on vesting schedules, exercise costs, taxation, share-sale restrictions, and post-listing market performance.
items.title: Anthropic IPO could create 2,800 millionaires as junior staff may out-earn senior executives

items.summary: Aarin Capital Chairman Mohandas Pai challenged Uday Kotak, founder of Kotak Mahindra Bank, on Thursday regarding the latter's comparison between AI company Anthropic's reported $1.5 trillion valuation and India's largest companies. Pai questioned why leading Indian bankers were not investing more aggressively in innovation and deep technology. Writing on X, he dismissed the comparison as inappropriate, stating that every disruption creates new companies with huge valuations because it is simply the nature of markets, adding that comparing such figures was silly.
items.title: Mohandas Pai responds to Uday Kotak over Anthropic's $1.5 trillion valuation

items.summary: The International Energy Agency reported Thursday that carbon emissions linked to global data centers are projected to rise about 70% by 2030, as growing demand for artificial intelligence drives electricity consumption higher. In its annual World Energy Outlook 2026 report, the Paris-based agency projected that global electricity consumption by data centers would double to about 1,000 terawatt-hours by 2030, with AI accounting for much of the increase. Data centers house the computer servers used to run AI systems and other digital services, requiring large amounts of electricity to operate and keep equipment cool. The expansion is expected to increase demand for electricity generated from fossil fuels, particularly in the United States and China, contributing to higher carbon emissions. The IEA projected that natural gas would supply about 60% of electricity used by US data centers by 2030, while coal would account for roughly half of the power consumed by China's AI data centers. In the European Union, renewable energy is expected to provide about 70% of data center electricity needs by the end of the decade. The agency also warned that rapid growth in electricity demand from AI infrastructure was putting additional pressure on power grids and equipment supply chains, highlighting the need for investment in electricity networks.
items.title: IEA projects 70% rise in data center carbon emissions by 2030

items.summary: Microsoft chief executive Satya Nadella said in an interview with CNBC's Jim Cramer that the company should have detected and contained a software flaw responsible for taking Outlook offline last week. He noted the defect only surfaced under a particular pattern of traffic, added "of course, we should have done the testing before," and argued Microsoft ought to have designed its systems so a failure in one part could be isolated before spreading globally. The outage disrupted email at businesses relying on Outlook for day-to-day communication. Nadella also raised a broader problem facing companies running older infrastructure: AI tools can help engineers identify flaws and develop fixes faster, but each fix still has to be tested and installed, and more frequent updates can make existing systems less stable. He described this as a trade-off software providers face while accelerating patch releases and keeping widely used services online, noting "there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that's unpatchable," citing firmware on chillers and HVAC systems connected to the internet. The interview followed Microsoft's Ignite conference pitch for Copilot as the main interface across its business software; a September overhaul consolidated AI tools into one app and introduced usage-based charges for advanced features, giving Microsoft another revenue source if customers buy fewer licences than it typically sells through per-employee arrangements. Nadella said usage already accounts for a substantial part of Dynamics, which handles sales and enterprise planning functions, and that Copilot can direct requests to models from Anthropic, OpenAI or Microsoft itself as its relationship with OpenAI evolves. On local opposition to data centre construction, he said companies must show residents what they gain, pointing to Quincy, Washington, where Microsoft has operated a data centre for about two decades and tax revenue helped fund a school and other public facilities. He also addressed Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia, a major Azure chip supplier, calling Huang a "singular founder" while saying Microsoft remained keen to work with interim chief executive Colette Kress, a former Microsoft employee, leaving Nvidia's board to decide what comes next.
items.title: Nadella says Microsoft should have caught Outlook bug before global outage

items.summary: The International Energy Agency (IEA) reported Thursday that global demand for cooling buildings has overtaken demand for heating for the first time, attributing the shift to rising temperatures and higher household incomes. In its World Energy Outlook 2026, published in Istanbul on November 19, 2026, the agency noted that increasing incomes are making air conditioning more accessible, particularly in emerging and developing economies. The report highlighted a stark gap: outside China, 85% of households in these regions face high temperatures yet fewer than one in five owns an air conditioner. Under the IEA's Stated Policies Scenario, global electricity consumption for cooling is projected to rise by 1,700 terawatt-hours by 2035, a projection that already incorporates a gradual increase in average global temperatures. The agency warned that more intense, frequent and prolonged heat waves could push this figure significantly higher as households buy air conditioners and use them more often; under such conditions the projected increase could reach approximately 2,400 terawatt-hours by 2035, about 40% above the stated policies projection. This additional demand would strain electricity grids during peak periods when large numbers of households require cooling simultaneously. Air conditioning is one factor among several driving global electricity consumption, alongside industrial motors, electric vehicles, heat pumps and data centers. Since 2019, global electricity demand has grown by an average of 3.3% annually, more than double the 1.5% yearly growth in overall energy demand. Meeting this rising demand will require substantial investment in power infrastructure; the IEA estimated that at least 25 million kilometers of new power lines are needed worldwide over the next decade, and another 15 million kilometers of existing transmission and distribution lines must be upgraded or replaced.
items.title: Global Building Cooling Demand Overtakes Heating for First Time, IEA Reports

items.summary: As Anthropic prepares its initial public offering, seven co-founders who left OpenAI five years ago could each see their fortunes rise into the billions. The company plans to sell shares between $70 and $78 each, potentially valuing it at more than $1 trillion (€911.61 billion), placing it alongside Walmart and JPMorgan Chase and above Coca-Cola, IBM, Starbucks, Delta Air Lines and General Motors combined. If the IPO price reaches $78 (€71), each founder's shareholding could be worth at least $18.5bn (€16.86 billion). Dario Amodei, 43-year-old CEO who left OpenAI in 2020 citing concerns about commercial interests overriding AI safety, founded the company with his sister Daniela and five colleagues; she is now president after studying English literature at UC Santa Cruz and working for Matt Cartwright's office and Stripe. Tom Brown oversees computing resources following work on GPT-3 at Google DeepMind and OpenAI. Jared Kaplan directs scientific research while teaching physics scaling laws at Johns Hopkins University, having earned his Harvard PhD in physics. Chris Olah leads interpretability research after time at Google Brain and OpenAI, receiving a Thiel Fellowship before completing his degree at the University of Toronto. Jack Clark brings a journalism background from ZDNet UK, The Register and Bloomberg to lead public benefit work through the Anthropic Institute; he is the only founder born outside North America, having grown up in Brighton, UK. Sam McCandlish serves as chief architect on AI system design and risk policies after OpenAI safety work, holding PhDs from Stanford and undergraduate degrees from Brandeis University.
items.title: Anthropic founders' wealth set to surge with company's IPO

items.summary:
The official Amazon Black Friday sale launched on November 19, beginning at 12:01 a.m. PT / 3:01 a.m. ET with millions of price drops across electronics, home goods, apparel, gaming gear, and more. The event is framed as a 12-day run extending through Thanksgiving and Cyber Monday, though the official Black Friday sale itself ends on Saturday, November 28 at 3:00 a.m. ET before transitioning into its weekend-long Cyber Monday promotion. Throughout the period Amazon offers daily themed deal drops of up to 60% off.

Apple deals include AirPods Pro 3 now $179 (regularly $249), an even lower price on AirPods Max 2 at $429 ($120 off, regularly $549), AirTag 2 packs matching all-time lows of $23 for a single unit and $70 for four units, the Apple Watch Series 12 lineup ranging from $329 to $479 with regular prices up to $60 higher, MacBook Neo starting at $650 (regularly $700), M5 MacBook Air models discounted by $200 or $250 depending on configuration, and the Apple Pencil (USB-C) at $69 (regularly $79). Amazon Devices offers include its all-new Android Alexa Tablets from $150 all-time lows, plus Fire TV Stick 4K down to $20 (regularly $60), a Fire TV Cube for $90 (regularly $200), and various other Fire TV models. Google deals feature up to $100 off the Pixel Watch 5 lineup with specific prices of $300, $330, $400, and $430 depending on size and connectivity, plus as much as $450 off the Pixel 11 series phones starting at $699 (regularly $899) for the base model. Samsung offers include up to $450 off its Z Fold 8 lineup with specific prices of $1,550 and $1,750 for the 256GB and 512GB models respectively against regular prices of $1,900 and $2,100, alongside S26 Ultra phones discounted from $950 to $1,150.

PlayStation deals include DualSense controllers from $55 (regularly $75+), a DualSense Edge controller for $170 (regularly $200), the PULSE Elite headset at $110 (regularly $150), and numerous game titles discounted by roughly half their regular prices. The article notes that many notable offers are not highlighted on Amazon's main sale page, directing readers to 9to5Toys.com for curated deals.

Regarding whether better deals will appear next week, the source states it is possible with additional products added each day through Thanksgiving and Black Friday, but asserts that big-ticket items tend to drop when the sale begins and see only minor price reductions as it progresses. The document contains no tables or figures requiring visualization.
items.title: Amazon's Official 2026 Black Friday Sale Launches

items.summary:
The Gentlemen ransomware group has added NVIDIA to its dark web data leak site, though it has not yet provided proof of a breach. The operation lists a countdown ending on November 28 and threatens to release stolen data if demands are met. In response, NVIDIA told BleepingComputer that it found no indication its systems or networks were affected but is now investigating an incident that may have impacted one of its service providers. A spokesperson stated: "NVIDIA is investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner." The Gentlemen emerged last year as a closed ransomware group before switching to a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, offering affiliates up to 90% of ransom proceeds compared with the typical 70%-80%. It operates as a double-extortion group, exfiltrating data from victims' networks before encrypting systems and threatening online leaks. Since its emergence, it has claimed more than 1,100 victims across manufacturing, healthcare, transportation, energy, education, financial services, and other sectors. NVIDIA separately confirmed two earlier breaches: in May this year, some Armenian users' information including names, email addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth, and usernames was exposed after a regional GeForce NOW Alliance partner was hacked, though the breach did not affect NVIDIA's network or operated services; and in March 2022, an attack claimed by the Lapsus$ gang affected more than 71,000 employees. The article also includes promotional content for Adaptive Security email protection tools.

No visual: separate facts about distinct incidents with no comparison across names.
items.title: NVIDIA Investigating Gentlemen Ransomware Breach Claims

items.summary: A letter to a forum, signed by Tan Lee Noi, advocates for integrating empathy-based moral education and critical thinking into the primary school curriculum. The author argues that children are born with a natural capacity for empathy, which should be nurtured early as it is essential for social and emotional development. Teaching students to respect and care for vulnerable sentient beings—including their peers and animals—is presented as a way to build emotional intelligence and perspective-taking ability. Citing research, the letter claims these competencies reduce classroom aggression, bullying, and antisocial behaviour, producing a safer learning environment. The author further contends that empathy education is most effective when paired with critical thinking, which teaches students to question assumptions, recognise biases, and evaluate motivations in order to resist peer pressure and misinformation. Together, the two approaches are said to benefit the wider community by fostering kinder, more resilient, and socially responsible citizens.
items.title: Letter advocating empathy and critical thinking in primary education

items.summary: A series of major technology outages struck over a week in November, prompting lawmakers to demand explanations and leaving users uncertain about the cause. The disruptions affected very different systems: Microsoft's email services went down on November 12 after two days of failures, with Downdetector logging 130,000 reports of Outlook problems at peak; Microsoft traced the failure to a latent software defect in its networking gateway servers worsened by changes in network traffic and reduced server capacity. The next day, around 3:30 pm ET, the Federal Aviation Administration halted all air travel across the US until about 8:30 pm, stranding tens of thousands; the FAA later said a faulty router installed the week before caused the shutdown and has since stopped installing new routers at its telecom sites. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy admitted finding the router took longer than he would have liked and put contractor L3Harris on notice, while officials dismissed rumors that artificial intelligence triggered the outage. On November 16, JPMorgan Chase customers faced delayed transactions due to a software bug in an on-premises hardware system, with Downdetector logging more than 20,000 reports of problems by mid-afternoon; other banks including Truist and Capital One also drew complaints. A day later, Apple reported an outage affecting its App Store, Apple Pay, Apple Music, AppleCare services, and iCloud sign-in after an internal update, with the company saying all platforms had since returned to normal. Beyond these four visible incidents, outages between November 12 and 16 also hit Anthropic's Claude, Workday, AWS's us-east-1 region, United Airlines, Marriott's website and apps, and systems at the National Security Agency. Officials say the incidents appear unrelated with no sign of a coordinated cyberattack, though some causes remain unclear; what they share is dependence on a handful of platforms and legacy networks that let a single fault spread quickly. Separately, Pakistan's telecom regulator said on November 18 that a fault in the SEA-ME-WE 5 undersea cable about 11 km off its coast could cause intermittent connectivity and slower service while traffic was rerouted during an investigation. Lawmakers have called for briefings at federal agencies, the FAA's review of its router failure is continuing, and fuller explanations from Microsoft, Chase, and others may reveal whether the week reflected bad luck or deeper systemic weakness.
items.title: Back-to-Back Tech Outages Raise Reliability Concerns

items.summary: Utkarsh Somaiya and Lewis Holden examine why estimates of GDP damages from climate change vary so widely, concluding that the largest source of uncertainty is how temperature changes are translated into economic damages rather than uncertainty about future temperatures themselves. They distinguish two broad categories: uncertainty within climate science and uncertainty in economic damage functions. Within climate science they identify scenario uncertainty (unknown future greenhouse gas emissions driven by technology, demographics and consumption), model uncertainty (different assumptions and parameters across climate models) and randomness from the inherent variability of the climate system. The relative importance of these sources depends on geographic scale, variable and time horizon; over short horizons and small areas randomness dominates temperature projections, while over longer horizons model and scenario uncertainty dominate as randomness averages out at a global level. Economic damage functions are simplified reduced-form relationships that translate variables such as average temperatures into damages without modelling structural mechanisms or economic adaptation. There is also disagreement about which variables to use in these relationships and how climate affects outputwhether it continuously suppresses the level of output, reduces long-term growth, manifests as periodic catastrophic shocks, or combines all of these effectswhich means there is no consensus on the basic relationship between climate change and damages. The authors quantify the relative importance using a framework based on temperature pathways from all IPCC scenarios combined with damage function specifications derived by Howard and Sterner (2025) through meta-analysis. Feeding scenario temperatures into level-effect damage functions yields an initial range of 0% to -7% of GDP driven purely by climate scenario uncertainty, while model uncertainty within a single scenario is captured separately; randomness has little effect on global damages. Introducing the full range of plausible damage functions widens the total estimate to between 1% and -37%, with the range expanding further into the future because these functions assume each additional degree of warming causes more damage than the previous one, confirming that damage function uncertainty is the dominant driver. The authors note some uncertainties can be reduced over time but argue reducing them will take time; waiting for excessive certainty risks delaying decisions. They recommend precautionary action and building resilience to plausible catastrophic outcomes rather than relying on models under deep uncertainty. Table A addresses which sources of uncertainty are reducible, though its contents are not detailed in the text. The authors clarify that these views are their own as Bank Underground contributors and do not necessarily reflect those of the Bank of England or its policy committees.
items.title: Sources of uncertainty in climate damage estimates

items.summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launches globally on November 19, and estimates from Sensor Tower place roughly three-quarters of the 17 million units sold so far on PlayStation, outselling Xbox. Shares in Sony rose almost 3% in Tokyo against a flat benchmark index. Analysts expect this worldwide enthusiasm to fall short in Japan, where Nintendo dominates gaming devices with its Switch 2 and consumers favor anime-style titles over realistic Western games. Toyo Securities analyst Hideki Yasuda said the current Japanese trends do not suit such a game and that there is no need for it to sell strongly at home; he added that Sony's benefits from royalties will be enormous while showing little desire to aggressively push hardware sales. In early 2026, Sony scored global success with Spider-Man: Brand New Day but faced competition in Japan from Chiikawa The Movie: The Secret Of Mermaid Island. Sorataka Goto of Kantan Games noted that Japanese gamers may struggle with the game's satirical elements and Western references, though worldwide hype is spilling over into unprecedented marketing for a Western-made title, including a large poster featuring characters Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval in Akihabara; he predicted GTA VI would not become a mega blockbuster but will do very well. Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 units during the July-September quarter, down from 4 million a year earlier, which analysts see as demand ahead of GTA VI. Bernstein analyst David Dai wrote that PlayStation profits are modelled materially higher in coming quarters on account of the launch, and the release bolsters Sony's slate after it delayed God Of War Laufey by three months to May 2027; Sony is also grappling with procurement challenges as memory chip costs have risen sharply due to the AI boom. Goto said a few friends bought GTA VI at midnight but he was not in a hurry, since it is only on PS5 and Xbox and multiplayer online is unavailable yet, though he would consider buying once it reaches PC; he separately praised Nintendo's Switch 2 remake of The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time, which has sold more than five million copies in the first four days after its November launch.
items.title: GTA VI's Japanese market prospects amid Sony windfall

items.summary: An Instagram advertisement for pistols exposed an illegal firearms trade in Pune, prompting a raid by Wagholi police in the Kesanand area that resulted in three arrests and one detention of a minor. Two of the arrested men had travelled from Goa to Pune to purchase weapons after finalising a deal through social media. Police seized four country-made pistols, four magazines, and 15 live cartridges from the suspects, collectively valued at ₹4,18,500. The identified individuals are Akash alias Gajya Ashok More, 21, of Navratna Society in Vadgaon Sheri; Manish Dilip Fernandes, 26; and Chandreshwar Mallesh, 21, both residents of Chandor in Margao, Goa. A minor was also detained in connection with the case. The operation began after Police Constable Pradeep Mote received a tip-off while patrolling, alerting him that three to four people carrying pistols were waiting on the road toward Jogeshwari Hill. Acting on this information, a team led by Police Sub-Inspector Shivshankar Raghu rushed to the location and detained the suspects. During investigation, police found that More had posted an offer for pistols on Instagram, prompting Fernandes from Goa to contact him and negotiate the purchase; after agreeing, Fernandes and his associate travelled to Kesanand to complete the transaction. Police also reported that More allegedly procured the firearms from Madhya Pradesh and had a prior criminal case registered against him for alleged pistol possession. A case has been filed at Wagholi Police Station under relevant Arms Act provisions, with further investigation underway to establish the weapons' source and identify others in the supply network.
items.title: Instagram Firearms Deal Leads to Pune Arrests

items.summary: On Nov 19, the High Court approved a $391.9 million collective sale of the leasehold rear block of The Centrepoint at 176A Orchard Road in Singapore. This followed reports that the Strata Titles Board had issued a stop order in August after two objections to the sale. After the board's decision, the collective sale committee applied to the High Court for approval. Before the Nov 19 hearing, the objecting owners Tanxuan Investments and an individual named Chin Yun Hee withdrew their objections. Lawyers for Tanxuan declined to comment on the nature of those objections due to confidentiality obligations, while Frasers Property and marketing agent Savills Singapore did not specify them either when asked. Observers note that common objections involve disputes over proceeds apportionment or collective sale price, or unit holders believing the sale was not conducted in good faith. On Feb 26, Frasers Property through its subsidiary Frasers Property Cuppage won the $391.9 million tender for the leasehold rear block. Under the agreed apportionment method, retail unit owners stand to receive between $840,000 and $9.29 million each, while apartment owners are expected to get between $2.65 million and $7.11 million per unit, subject to final adjustments. The Centrepoint was completed in 1983 and comprises a freehold front plot and the leasehold rear plot containing 66 retail units and 66 residential apartments on about 44,700 sq ft of land zoned commercial with a gross plot ratio of 5.6 and maximum height up to 10 storeys. The site occupies prime Orchard Road space with a direct sheltered link to Somerset MRT station. Frasers Property already held more than 52% of the rear block units by strata area before this sale, owns about 96% of the freehold front plot units, and fully owns 51 Cuppage Road, a connected 10-storey office building. A spokesperson said the acquisition strengthens its Orchard Road position and supports the government's masterplan to transform the precinct into a premier lifestyle destination. Savills Singapore managing director Jeremy Lake described this as the firm's fifth Orchard Road collective sale in recent years, with combined transaction value totalling nearly $2.7 billion. Separately, on Aug 31 Frasers announced its acquisition of Cuppage Terrace, a cluster of 17 conservation shophouses next to The Centrepoint for an agreed property value of $175 million, covering about 34,678 sq ft of gross floor area excluding the outdoor refreshment area. Savills Singapore's Jeremy Lake noted this marks its fifth Orchard Road collective sale in recent years with combined transaction value totalling nearly $2.7 billion.
items.title: High Court approves $391.9m collective sale of The Centrepoint's leasehold rear block

items.summary: Photographer-turned-entrepreneur Sha Hao relocated from Shanghai to Sydney to establish a virtual production studio, working alongside an Australian director who serves as his creative partner. The pair employ LED screens and virtual filming technology to produce short films for clients based in the United States. This arrangement is presented as demonstrating how China's hardware and software capabilities can be combined with Australia's creative talent to build a film production network spanning the Pacific Ocean.
items.title: Shanghai-to-Sydney Virtual Production Studio

items.summary: Despite an India-UK trade agreement that came into effect in July and reduced tariffs on Scotch whisky from 150% to 75%, a dispute over customs classification has left thousands of litres of bulk Scotch stuck at Indian ports. The disagreement centres on whether bulk Scotch concentrates qualify for the concessional tariff or should be classified as raw material under a newly created category called "compound alcoholic preparations," which attracts a 150% tariff, with an additional consumption tax pushing the effective duty to 162.5%. Indian investigators argue that bulk Scotch is merely a raw material used in manufacturing and therefore does not qualify for reduced tariffs, while liquor companies including Pernod Ricard, Diageo, and Bacardi contend that all Scotch imports should receive the 75% rate regardless of whether they are bottled or brought in bulk. The dispute has left more than 80 shipping containers belonging to these three companies blocked at Indian ports. To secure provisional release while investigations continue, companies can pay duty equivalent to 75% of goods value upfront and cover the remainder through bank guarantees; Pernod Ricard and Diageo have moved to arrange such funding, while Bacardi was still considering its next steps. The arrangement adds pressure on working capital, with smaller manufacturers facing greater difficulties as they may need collateral and must report these guarantees as contingent liabilities. Bulk Scotch imports are central to India's whisky industry, accounting for around 80% of British Scotch imports by volume, most used to produce Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) blended whiskies sold at lower prices than fully imported brands such as Chivas Regal and Johnnie Walker. The UK government has repeatedly stated it is working with New Delhi to resolve the issue, with a spokesperson telling Reuters that ministers were "urgently working with the government of India to resolve this issue." The Scotch Whisky Association estimated 2024 exports stood at $335 million and forecast the trade agreement could increase exports by $1.34 billion over five years.
items.title: India-UK Trade Dispute Blocks Bulk Scotch Whisky Imports

items.summary:
Based on advance calculations by NASA, its Voyager 1 probe is believed to have reached a distance of one light-day from Earth approximately Wednesday at 5:16 a.m. ET (1016 GMT), marking a milestone no other spacecraft has achieved. The distance corresponds to about 26 billion kilometers, the span light travels in 24 hours. Because signals travel at the speed of light, JPL officials must wait roughly a day for confirmation from the probe and have scheduled an event on Thursday to discuss the achievement. Voyager project manager Suzanne Dodd called reaching one light-day "an astounding feat" she never expected to witness.

The spacecraft was launched in 1977 and is now the most distant human-made object, traveling at nearly 61,000 kilometers per hour. It crossed into interstellar space by passing through the heliosphere's outer edge in 2012; its twin, Voyager 2, also launched in 1977, entered interstellar space in 2018.

A JPL representative noted that recent power-saving measures may allow both Voyagers to remain in communication with Earth for three to four more years. The mission's goal is scientific research, and there is enough power to sustain the current instruments through next year's 50th launch anniversary; beyond that remains uncertain given the spacecraft are nearly 50 years old.

Voyager 1 continues gathering data after passing Jupiter and Saturn earlier in its journey. Its instruments have detected a faint hum from gas vibrations in interstellar space, while continuously transmitting measurements of magnetic fields, cosmic rays, and plasma waves whenever the Deep Space Network points an antenna at it. Dodd reported that after crossing the heliopause, the magnetic field direction did not rotate into the expected interstellar orientation but has instead retained its sun-governed direction; the team is watching for when rotation occurs. She also noted ongoing effects from solar activity, including coronal mass ejections whose shocks and pressure fronts reach Voyager 1 and beyond, prompting the question of where the sun's influence ends and pristine interstellar space begins.
items.title: NASA Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day Milestone

items.summary: Writing as an editor's note that his views do not necessarily reflect CGTN, Xin Ge of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics argues that global bay areas could provide the Asia-Pacific with practical platforms for cooperation amid rising protectionism. At the opening of the APEC CEO Summit 2026 on Wednesday morning at Shenzhen's Qianhai International Convention Center, President Xi Jinping called for establishing a global association for bay-area economic cooperation to strengthen exchanges among world-wide bay areas and explore deeper Asia-Pacific economic ties. Ge contends this initiative could complement APEC by translating regional consensus into concrete projects through closer links among ports, industrial parks, financial institutions and research centers, with examples including coordinated digital customs procedures and greener shipping, cross-border green investment, and joint research in artificial intelligence, biomedicine and advanced manufacturing. He emphasizes that the association's value depends on easing practical cross-border challenges such as customs procedures, product certification, payment arrangements and access to legal services rather than relying on summit declarations alone. The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area is positioned as a natural anchor given its concentration of advanced manufacturing, universities, capital markets and international professional services across Shenzhen's innovation strengths, the Pearl River Delta's industrial base, Macao's cultural and tourism assets, and Hong Kong's links to global finance and business networks. Ge notes that for the region cooperation must move beyond physical connectivity toward harmonizing rules governing research funding, professional qualifications, commercial data and financial services while maintaining safeguards. He highlights Hong Kong's approaching 30th anniversary of its return on July 1, 2027 as an opportunity to leverage its complementary strengths in financing projects, structuring international transactions, resolving disputes and connecting mainland enterprises with overseas investors for green infrastructure, joint research and company expansion. Ge cautions that expectations should remain prudent since the association is still a proposal whose membership, mandate and working methods are undefined, it should complement rather than duplicate APEC or existing networks, and its benefits must extend beyond large corporations to smaller businesses, researchers and young entrepreneurs. He suggests a practical starting agenda of startup exchange programs, joint research funds, recognition of green-finance standards, digital trade facilitation and regular exchanges among port authorities and universities, with progress measured against public benchmarks rather than ambitious announcements. Ge concludes that the association's success will depend on making cross-border cooperation easier and more sustainable to turn regional commitments into tangible business outcomes as bay areas rely on open channels for trade, talent and investment.
items.title: China Proposes Global Bay-Area Economic Cooperation Association

items.summary: The People's Bank of China (PBOC) announced on Wednesday that it had signed the China-Canada Financial Working Group Terms of Reference with Canada's Department of Finance and the Bank of Canada. The signing clarifies the participating authorities, areas of cooperation, and communication methods for the working group, which is intended to operate regularly and institutionalized while strengthening communication between the two countries' financial regulators and deepening mutually beneficial sectoral cooperation. The group was established in January following a consensus reached by China's and Canada's leaders that year, with its first meeting held in Beijing in April. It will focus exchanges on developments in the financial sector, monetary policy, regulatory policies and practices, financial markets, financial stability, fintech, anti-money laundering and countering financing of terrorism, cross-border financial flows, and global financial governance. The two sides agreed to enhance collaboration by testing and discussing use of their recently renewed bilateral currency swap agreement, exploring expanded local-currency use in trade and investment, encouraging two-way investment, and promoting discussions on green and sustainable finance under multilateral platforms. They have already conducted technical exchanges on panda bond issuance, cross-border payment efficiency, anti-money laundering, and countering financing of terrorism. Both sides welcomed steps by the PBOC and Bank of Canada to implement their bilateral local currency swap arrangement; both welcomed eligible Canadian institutions issuing panda bonds in China, while Canada also welcomes and supports China's interest in issuing RMB-denominated green sovereign bonds in the Canadian market.
items.title: China-Canada Financial Working Group Signs Terms of Reference

items.summary: As Silicon Valley figures increasingly become subjects of Hollywood productions, Sam Altman, founder and CEO of OpenAI, is set to appear as himself in the biographical comedy-drama 'Artificial,' starring Andrew Garfield. The film chronicles OpenAI's rise alongside the internal turmoil that followed his brief ousting from the company in 2023, with a theatrical release scheduled for Christmas. Speaking at the New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Altman said he was no longer struck by the prospect of being portrayed in a movie, noting it would have seemed very strange to him two decades ago but is now among the least surprising things about his life. He identified what he considers genuinely weird: ushering in technology while carrying significant responsibility for its success amid real concerns. The article also contrasts Altman's reaction with Mark Zuckerberg's response to 'The Social Network,' which depicted Facebook's founding and, per Zuckerberg, mischaracterized his motivations despite accurate details like clothing. Zuckerberg reportedly organized a company outing when the film released and purchased an Ardsley High School T-shirt worn by co-star Jesse Eisenberg at auction, while Eisenberg has distanced himself from being associated with Zuckerberg. Regarding Garfield, who is known for Spider-Man and previously played Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin in 'The Social Network,' Altman had not yet been interviewed about the film as of publication.
items.title: Sam Altman Unfazed by Andrew Garfield Portrayal in 'Artificial'

items.summary: Snapchat announced on Wednesday that it is enabling developers to build AR Lenses using their existing AI coding assistants, including Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex. Snapchat Lenses are augmented reality effects used across the platform to alter appearance, add digital objects, or create interactive camera experiences. The company introduced Easy Lens CLI as an extension of its earlier Easy Lens tool, which lets creators generate Lenses from a single prompt on web and mobile; the new command-line version brings that same approach into developers' existing workflows so AI assistants handle technical work while creators focus on vision. Snapchat frames the launch as a way to lower barriers for AR content creation and reach more developers who increasingly rely on AI coding tools, rather than requiring them to learn Snapchat's own development environment. Creators enrolled in Snapchat's Lens+ Payouts program can earn money from Lenses built with Easy Lens CLI; the company reported paying out $1.8 million to Lens+ community creators last month. According to Snapchat, developers describe their desired Lens in plain language and the AI assistant manages the full process: building using more than 100 AR building blocks and 50 AI asset generators, generating previews, publishing to Snapchat, and tracking performance. The tool reportedly supports Web Lens games with leaderboards as well as camera effects and beauty filters, and can move a game from initial idea to published Lens within a single day without developers writing code themselves. Snapchat says the capability lets AI assistants generate assets, build and test Lenses, address errors, and send updated versions directly to a creator's phone. The tool is aimed at multiple creator types: game developers who can bring existing browser games as Web Lenses, AI creators using assets from their preferred tools in their own style, and agencies or brands that can convert campaign videos, images, and other brand assets into AR experiences with less production time. Easy Lens CLI runs on Mac, Windows, and Linux.
items.title: Snapchat Adds AI Coding Assistants to Its Lens Creation Tooling

items.summary:
The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways revised pollution under control (PUC) certificate rules through the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, which amend Rule 115(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. Notified on November 13 and effective upon publication in the Official Gazette, the amendment replaces a system that set validity primarily by Bharat Stage emission category with one based on vehicle age and whether the vehicle is used privately or commercially. It also standardises testing intervals across states, replacing regional variations.

Under the earlier rules, all private BS-VI vehicles received certificates valid for 12 months regardless of age; commercial BS-VI vehicles likewise had a uniform year-long validity. The new framework introduces three age-based brackets for both categories. For private BS-VI vehicles: up to six years old receive three-year certificates (up from one), those aged more than six and up to ten years keep 12-month validity, and those older than ten years drop to six months. Commercial BS-VI vehicles get shorter extensions; the first bracket rises to two years instead of three, while the middle bracket stays at 12 months and the over-ten-years bracket falls to six months.

For older emission standards, the amendment imposes uniform intervals nationwide: all BS-I, II and III vehicles now require certificates valid for three months regardless of age or category, aligning with Delhi's existing requirement. BS-IV vehicles move from a 12-month central provision to a standard six-month validity across private and commercial use.

The rules also clarify renewal timing: if testing occurs within the ten days before expiry, the renewed certificate takes effect from the previous one's expiry date; if tested on or after expiry, it becomes valid from the test date. Certificates issued before the amendment remain valid until their original expiry dates, and owners need not obtain fresh certificates immediately - new validity applies only at first renewal under the amended rules.

The article notes that all vehicles must hold a certificate from an authorised state testing centre, verifiable digitally through the Parivahan PUCC Portal. It also flags uncertainty: earlier provisions exempted new vehicles across emission categories from obtaining a separate PUC for their first year after registration, but the amendment does not clarify whether this exemption has been retained or altered.
items.title: India shortens and standardises PUC certificate validity by vehicle age

items.summary: The BJP launched a broadside against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi on Thursday over remarks he made at an event in Chicago. BJP leaders claimed that Rahul had called Indian democracy "sick," but the video released by news agencies showed him instead describing the democracy as "sacred." The exchange occurred during an interaction with students at the University of Chicago, where Rahul was asked why the opposition does not boycott elections if it believes they are being rigged. He responded that their strategy is to expose what is happening and take a beating until people in India realize that the system has been fully demolished. BJP leader Bhandari condemned the remarks, stating that Rahul had again proven he loves his family's party while hating democracy, and called him the "Leader of Anti India Propaganda," arguing that every time Rahul speaks this way he shows himself to be against the Indian state, its people, and its democratic fabric. The article was written by Rohitashwa Ranjan, a digital journalist with The Times of India who covers elections, party dynamics, and politics beneath headlines.
items.title: BJP accuses Rahul Gandhi of calling Indian democracy 'sick'

items.summary:
The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) ruled in favour of wind power generators on November 17, 2026, setting aside a batch of 23 appeals challenging orders issued by the Andhra Pradesh Electricity Regulatory Commission (APERC). The tribunal held that generators are entitled to receive the applicable agreed tariff for all electricity supplied to distribution companies, regardless of whether annual generation exceeds the normative Capacity Utilisation Factor (CUF).

The dispute arose from Power Purchase Agreements between wind power developers and the Southern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited (APSPDCL). Under APERC's tariff orders, generic tariffs were set on a normative CUF basis; for example, its November 15, 2012 order fixed a tariff of ₹4.70 per unit based on a normative CUF of 23% over 25 years from the Commercial Operation Date. However, through several orders issued between September 2022 and July 2024, APERC treated the normative CUF as a payment limit, directing that electricity generated beyond this benchmark receive only ₹0.50 per unit, along with provisions for cumulative annual CUF adjustments.

Wind power developers challenged these directions before APTEL; one case involved Beta Wind Farm Private Limited disputing restrictions on payments for electricity supplied between July 2016 and July 2017. The distribution companies filed cross-appeals arguing that excess generation should either remain unpaid or be addressed through fresh tariff proceedings.

The APTEL bench, comprising Judicial Member Virender Bhat and Technical Member Ajay Talegaonkar, examined whether APERC had authority to introduce different payment arrangements for electricity generated beyond the normative CUF. The tribunal clarified that normative CUF is an annual benchmark used only for calculating fixed costs and determining generic tariffs. Because wind generation depends on changing weather conditions and actual output can vary significantly year to year, the normative CUF cannot be treated as a separate billing limit or used to divide electricity into regular and excess categories.

The tribunal also observed that the PPAs contained no provision restricting payments to electricity generated within the normative CUF; instead they specified monthly limits based on contracted export capacity and operating hours rather than an annual generation cap. It further noted that wind developers already bear risks associated with lower wind availability and generation shortfalls, so restricting payments for additional electricity would discourage generators from supplying more power during favourable conditions.

Accordingly, APTEL set aside the ₹0.50 per unit payment provision and cumulative CUF adjustment directions, directing that all delivered electricity be paid at the applicable generic tariff under the respective PPAs. The tribunal rejected APSPDCL's request to remand the matter to APERC and ordered payment of withheld amounts along with applicable interest.
items.title: APTEL Rules Wind Generators Entitled to Full Tariff for Generation Beyond Normative CUF

items.summary: On Thursday morning, shares of air-conditioning makers rose as benchmark London Metal Exchange copper contracts fell to their lowest level since April 7. Voltas jumped more than 5% to Rs 1,192.90 apiece on the NSE, while Blue Star surged over 5% to Rs 1,709.10 apiece. PG Electroplast, which supplies components for air conditioners, rose around 6% to trade near Rs 571 apiece. The copper decline followed a stronger US dollar and growing concerns about Chinese industrial demand, with the selloff overshadowed by weakness in AI-linked stocks that had otherwise been tightening copper supply. A stronger dollar was attributed to Federal Reserve meeting minutes suggesting officials saw rising inflation risk while holding rates steady, along with hawkish comments from Kansas City Fed President Jeff Schmid warning that inflation remained too high and more action may be needed. CME's FedWatch tool priced a nearly 90% chance of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the December FOMC meeting, with a 10% probability of a larger 50-basis-point move. Analysts also linked falling copper to worries about China's economy and its prolonged property downturn, given the metal's heavy use in construction, electrical wiring and infrastructure. The AI-linked stock selloff added pressure as enthusiasm for new data centre spending cooled, even though copper is essential to that electrical infrastructure. Over the past week, Voltas gained 7% and Blue Star jumped 8%, while PG Electroplast recorded marginal weekly losses; over a month, Voltas rose 17%, Blue Star climbed 9% and PG Electroplast jumped 12%. The three stocks delivered returns in the range of 45-150% over three years. Axis Securities noted that FOMC minutes could shape the broader commodities outlook. The article was written by Debaroti Adhikary, who is not a SEBI-registered Research Analyst or Investment Adviser and holds no financial interest in the companies mentioned.
items.title: Falling copper prices lift Voltas and other AC stocks

items.summary:
Kemi Badenoch defended a remark she made to justify the Conservative plan to cut sickness and disability benefits by £14bn. At Prime Minister's Questions, Labour leader Andy Burnham had demanded that she withdraw her “double amputees run marathons” comment, calling it crass and insensitive. On the Today programme this morning, Badenoch rejected the criticism, insisting she was delivering a message of hope rather than an attack on disabled people. She argued that if anyone can work then they should be encouraged to do so, using her example to suggest those with ADHD and mild anxiety should return to work. When presenter Nick Robinson challenged her by saying it is unreasonable to use an exceptional case as a guide for most disabled people, Badenoch disagreed, stating that governments routinely use extreme examples to illustrate points. She accused Robinson of faux outrage and tone policing, adding that while others are free to disagree, she knew where she stood.

The broadcast also covered several other stories. Tulip Siddiq said she was considering legal action against the former interim leader of Bangladesh over corruption allegations from his administration that led to her resignation last year. On social media policy, Kemi Badenoch expressed concern about government intervention in getting a Russell Brand prison message video removed from YouTube, noting that while Brand had been convicted and is guilty under the law, his wife who posted the video was a separate person. Housing minister Matthew Pennycook confirmed the Ministry of Justice is in dialogue with Google over the removal but admitted they have no power to mandate it, since removal depends on the platform's own terms; Meta had already disabled Brand's Instagram and Facebook accounts after his conviction.

Badenoch also criticised a historic meeting between Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump in China, describing it as disturbing because the three leaders appeared to be trying to carve up the world into a tri-polar arrangement with Russia taking Europe. She went further than Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, who had been pressed by Ed Davey about the security implications of the meeting but stopped short of expressing concern.

The day's agenda included Louise Haigh answering questions in the Commons at 9.30am, James Cleverly expected to win more than 50% of the vote in the first round of Conservative voting for London mayor 2028, a Downing Street lobby briefing at 11.30am, Heather Hallett publishing her report on the test, trace and isolate system at noon, Chris Bryant attending a British-Irish Intergovernmental Conference meeting in Dublin, and Andy Burnham arriving in Berlin around 12.15pm for a pro-Ukraine coalition of the willing summit.
items.title: Badenoch Defends Amputee Comment on Disability Benefit Cuts

items.summary: The remaining Kerch rail bridge connecting Crimea to Russia was attacked overnight, halting train services two days after a Ukrainian air raid destroyed the adjacent road bridge. Sergei Aksyonov, the Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, announced on Wednesday night that another attack had occurred and added Thursday that trains would resume crossing from approximately 4pm. Emergency repair crews reportedly made heroic efforts to restore the track, and Russia's transport ministry said nobody was wounded. The raid came hours before an unprecedented three-way summit in Shenzhen between Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, and Xi Jinping. This marked the third time the $3.6bn bridge, built by Russia after its occupation of Crimea, had been struck within a week; on Tuesday a 227-metre section of the road spanning the Kerch strait was destroyed following a missile and drone attack planned over several weeks. Ukrainian military sources indicated the timing of the road bridge strike was deliberate ahead of the summit, suggesting the follow-up raid on the rail bridge may have been intended to bring it down as well. One source in Ukraine's armed forces said this week's attacks were designed to embarrass Putin globally, stating that destroying the bridge sends a message to Trump and Xi that Putin is not as strong as he pretends. For Ukraine, the bridge remains a hated symbol of Russian arrogance; Kyiv has declared it illegal and previously attempted twice to destroy it with a truck bomb in 2022 and a sea drone the following year. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy hailed his earlier attack on the road section as an unprecedented military operation that culminated a long campaign largely involving domestically produced drones and ballistic missiles, though he noted the railway line remained standing at that time. Flamingo FP-5 cruise missiles and Palianytsia drones struck the central road section bringing down its supporting arch, while Ukraine's Neptune cruise missile and the Ruta drone made by Dutch company Destinus targeted the adjacent rail section.
items.title: Kerch Rail Bridge Attacked Again Ahead of Trump-Putin-Xi Summit

items.summary: EDF Energy, owned by the French state and Britain's fourth-largest supplier, plans to complete its takeover of pay-as-you-go specialist Utilita early next year. The deal would add 1.3m accounts to EDF's customer base, growing its share of the UK household energy market to more than 6m accounts, while bringing on board Utilita's 1,500 staff at an undisclosed price. Both companies will continue serving customers independently until the transaction concludes, and Utilita clients will be contacted about any service changes; EDF intends to keep operating from Utilita's headquarters near Southampton, home to roughly 600 of its employees. The acquisition follows a deal completed a year earlier in which EDF took on 47,000 standard credit accounts from Utilita as it sought to sharpen its focus on smart pay-as-you-go customers. Simone Rossi, chief executive of EDF's UK business, said the takeover would bring further expertise and represent a significant step toward growing EDF's UK customer base, while founder Bill Bullen said Utilita could continue offering best-in-class smart prepay solutions. The deal is likely to have strengthened Utilita financially after it briefly fell short of Ofgem's tougher financial resilience tests in an assessment in September 2025; Utilita confirmed being one of five suppliers that failed the rules last year but complied within months of the regulator flagging its position. For EDF, the acquisition supports a business where most large suppliers are losing customers: EDF lost about 280,000 accounts in the year after July 2025, while British Gas, Scottish Power and E.ON Next also shed customers, with Octopus Energy as the only major supplier to grow its market share. Utilita was founded in 2003 and became the first supplier to install a smart meter in 2008, modernising pay-as-you-go by enabling top-ups via app, website or phone instead of at corner shops or post offices. The transaction follows German group E.ON Next's purchase of struggling rival Ovo last month after competition watchdog approval, as households brace for sharp winter bill rises; consultancy Cornwall Insight forecast the quarterly price cap would jump 26% from January to around £2,166 a year for a typical household.
items.title: EDF acquires Utilita in UK energy market consolidation

items.summary:
Survivors of a 2019 landslide in Bududa, an eastern Uganda district prone to landslides, have taken their case to the United Nations Human Rights Committee. The complainants number more than 50 killed, including 33 children, though the article reports two slightly different death tolls: one passage cites 'more than 50 people' and another specifies 'more than 53 people.' Forty-eight survivors filed complaints accusing the government of violating Uganda's constitution by failing to implement effective disaster management measures in Bududa. They argue that a relocation programme ignores their safety, land rights, and livelihoods.

The case is believed to be the first seeking climate adaptation measures globally, potentially setting precedent. Survivors say every heavy rain brings renewed fear of another tragedy; William Tsama, one claimant who lost four family members, framed his legal action as a lesson for victims ignored by governments. Uganda introduced a resettlement plan in 2011 with limited progress, and last month launched a new programme offering affected households 18 million Ugandan shillings ($4,300) to relocate.

Under the scheme, families can choose between two acres of land valued at 8 million shillings ($1,900), plus 10 million shillings (about $2,400) toward building a house, or take the equivalent land allowance in cash alongside the same housing grant. The programme is expected to benefit 1,410 households identified as living in high-risk areas.

The government has given residents of designated high-risk areas two months, from November to December, to leave or face forced eviction. Complainants say changing rainfall patterns and declining soil fertility have also damaged farming livelihoods. They seek compensation for lost family members and livelihoods, plus emergency measures including accessible early-warning systems in high-risk areas.

Survivors first launched legal action in 2020 and received support from the Ugandan environmental organisation Greenwatch three years later. Greenwatch Executive Director Samantha Atukunda Kakuru Mwesigwa said the case is about forcing government policy to keep pace with a changing climate, ensuring loss and damage is no longer an afterthought.

The article places Bududa within broader East African disaster trends: Kenya's floods and landslides killed at least 181 people between March and May 2024 per the Kenya Red Cross; Rwanda's floods and landslides killed 135 in May 2023; and a flash flood swept through Nepal's Gorkha district after a landslide blocked a river, killing over 1,500. ClientEarth lawyer Vesselina Newman said poorer countries contributing little to global emissions bear heavy consequences and need greater financial support from high-income nations.

The UN Human Rights Committee will ask the Ugandan government to respond within six months.
items.title: Uganda landslide survivors seek climate justice at UN

items.summary:
Tamil Nadu faces intensifying climate stress as El Niño is expected to worsen both drought and extreme rainfall risks across the state. The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) confirmed an 80-100% probability of a persistent El Niño phase extending into April 2027, with global warming raising baseline ocean temperatures and amplifying the cycle's effects on already climate-stressed regions like India.

Tamil Nadu relies heavily on monsoon inflows for water security: the southwest monsoon (June to September) replenishes reservoirs while the northeast monsoon (October to December) sustains rainfall. This year's southwest monsoon ended on September 30 with a 12.6% rainfall deficiency, the lowest since 2015, creating deficits over Western Ghats catchment areas and reducing reservoir inflows into Tamil Nadu.

Historically, India experienced 16 El Niño events between 1951 and 2025 lasting nine to 18 months each. Major Indian drought years occurred during strong El Niño periods in 1982, 1987, 2002, 2009, and 2015, with southwest monsoon deficiencies of 14.3% in 2015, 21.8% in 2009, and 19.2% in 2002.

A 52-year climate study (1971-2022) published in the International Journal of Climatology found that south peninsular India, including Tamil Nadu, is prone to drought as a long-term trend. TNAU projects normal northeast monsoon rainfall of 468 mm versus a seasonal average of 464 mm for 2026, offering only partial relief while El Niño may cause uneven distribution with intense coastal rainfall and drier interior conditions.

Agriculture in Tamil Nadu depends on the monsoons, and uneven rainfall makes rainfed systems vulnerable as reduced moisture lowers crop yields. Major crops including paddy, groundnut, maize, cotton, pulses, sugarcane, millets, and coconut are affected, along with livestock facing water stress and fodder shortages.

Districts flagged for El Niño vulnerability cluster in northern and central Tamil Nadu: Ariyalur, Perambalur, Tiruppattur, Vellore, Tiruchirappalli, Cuddalore, Kallakurichi, Kanchipuram, Ranipettai, Tiruvallur, Tiruvannamalai, Villupuram, and Pudukkottai. Agricultural districts draw water from upstream Karnataka, which weakens with a poor southwest monsoon, while interior rainfed areas depend on poorly maintained small reservoirs.

Groundwater remains heavily exploited but depleted; the Central Ground Water Board's 2025 assessment classified 103 of Tamil Nadu's 313 groundwater units as over-exploited. Coastal aquifers across nearly 1,076 kilometres spanning 14 coastal districts face seawater intrusion from sea level rise.

The Tamil Nadu government constituted an expert committee in July under the Disaster Management Act, 2005 to advise TNDRRA on El Niño preparedness. Activist G. Sundarrajan of Poovulagin Nanbargal says these recommendations remain unimplemented and urges restoring water resources "on a war footing." ICAR's District-wise Contingency Plan of 2026 places western and central Tamil Nadu districts in highly to medium vulnerable categories, recommending drought-tolerant crops, rainwater harvesting, soil moisture conservation, and improved irrigation.

Experts note El Niño can also bring intense rainfall causing floods, as seen historically. Akshay Deoras of the University of Reading observed early indications that coastal Tamil Nadu rainfall could improve in November and December 2026.
items.title: El Niño threatens to deepen Tamil Nadu's water stress and agricultural risk

items.summary: The international response to climate change remains inadequate, leaving vulnerable communities to absorb costs from disasters they did little to cause. The Fund for responding to Loss and Damage was created in 2022 after developing countries spent decades demanding financial support for destruction that cannot be prevented through emissions cuts or avoided through adaptation. In its first funding round, the fund received 176 requests from 119 countries seeking a total of $2.8 billion while setting aside only $342 million; an initial package is due before its board in December. Of the $822.71 million pledged by governments recorded in UN documents, just $485.77 million had been received by July 31, and the fund's first replenishment process will not begin until 2027. Harjeet Singh of the Fill the Fund campaign called it "a lifeboat with no oars," arguing that a few hundred million dollars in voluntary pledges cannot match the scale of destruction and that vulnerable countries need large-scale grants rather than loans that deepen debt. Nepal illustrates the gap: August floods from a glacier collapse killed more than 1,400 people, and while the World Bank estimates recovery will cost about $4.8 billion, the fund has provisionally set aside just $21.6 million, which is not yet disbursed money. Delays compound the problem because countries must prepare proposals and wait for approvals before funds are released, costing families shelter and farmers lost seasons. The urgency is acute in South Asia: Pakistan's Sindh province farmers remain dealing with 2022 floods that destroyed crops and homes; coastal Bangladesh faces saltwater intrusion, storm surges and erosion affecting health, culture and social ties; India confronts similar pressures along its coast, including the Sundarbans. On Pari Island near Jakarta, around 4,000 people live on just over 41 hectares after worsening tidal flooding since 2019 with a worst point in 2021. Four residents sued cement producer Holcim for compensation and emission reduction; the case was declared admissible in 2025 but the company has appealed, though liability remains unestablished. For Pacific islanders, rising seas threaten freshwater sources and places central to identity: Kirsten Madison of the Marshall Islands said land holds identities, languages and traditions, while Harjeet Singh added that existence cannot be put a price tag on. The fund can help families rebuild homes, farmers recover livelihoods and countries protect communities from repeated shocks, but it cannot restore lost land or replace uprooted cultures; this requires substantially more money, faster decisions and easier access to grants as negotiations continue in Antalya.
items.title: Climate loss and damage fund falls far short of needs

items.summary: Senegalese authorities are continuing search operations after a pirogue reportedly carrying around 100 migrants capsized off the coast near Yenne, south of Dakar. The vessel washed ashore badly damaged on Wednesday and was due to resume searches Thursday. Initial reports said one person had died, though local media reported at least four bodies recovered; dozens remain missing. Oumar Sow, a representative of the village chief, told AFP that cries could be heard from the boat even from the beach around 02:00 GMT. A survivor questioned by police said there were about 100 people aboard, including five women. Police recovered identity documents, several mobile phones and personal belongings, including a school enrolment document. This incident comes less than two weeks after a shipwreck off Thieppe killed at least 39 people in one of Senegal's deadliest migration disasters. At a cabinet meeting Wednesday, President Diomaye Faye expressed concern about renewed irregular departures by migrants hoping to reach Europe and instructed the interior ministry to prepare a report examining the factors driving these journeys and proposing measures to address them; he had previously urged citizens not to risk their lives on such crossings. The UN's IOM recorded at least 454 deaths and disappearances off the West African coast this year, warning the figure likely underestimates reality as many boats vanish without survivors or a trace. As North Africa routes tighten due to stronger European cooperation, migrants are increasingly targeting Spain's Canary Islands in overloaded wooden pirogues unsuited to long Atlantic voyages; most arrivals there this year are from Senegal, driven by limited employment, family pressures and established migration networks. On 7 November, El Hierro declared a state of emergency after more than 3,300 people arrived in about 30 boats since the month began, roughly a third of the island's population.
items.title: Migrant boat capsizes off Senegal, dozens missing

items.summary: A pattern has emerged across leading AI laboratories in which safety researchers and engineers are leaving their jobs to issue public warnings that commercial pressures are overriding safety guardrails. Last month, the person who oversaw safety reports for OpenAI's product releases quit because he described the company's culture as 'broken' and said the entire AI industry was too careless about developing the technology. The previous month, a researcher at Anthropic, an OpenAI rival, left warning that he believed AI 'could kill us all by the end of the decade'. Isabelle Ferreras argues these resignations reveal a deeper institutional failure: when exit becomes the only way for a conscientious engineer to raise the alarm, it signals broken corporate governance and takes with each departure the knowledge needed to steer systems safely. She notes that policymakers, tech workers, trade unionists, members of parliament, and experts from institutions including the Vatican and the UN are gathering in London this week to discuss AI safety, but contends regulation cannot be safe from outside if companies remain autocracies on the inside. Ferreras criticizes regulatory debates for treating AI either as a consumer product tested for defects or as a geopolitical race won by relaxing rules, citing Ursula von der Leyen's EU digital omnibus, which delays implementation of requirements in the 2024 AI Act covering 'high-risk' systems, at the encouragement of corporate lobbies arguing legislation imposes too many burdens. She stresses that AI is not merely software but a technology of government, and inside frontier labs such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and Google, executives and capital investors decide which values are coded into models shaping millions of lives. Referencing Jeremias Adams-Prassl's research on the gig economy and automated work in Europe, she notes algorithmic management already monitors, evaluates and dismisses workers without human oversight. Drawing on Daron Acemoglu and Simon Johnson, 2024 Nobel laureates in economics, Ferreras argues technological revolutions do not automatically produce shared prosperity because institutions decide who benefits and who pays; citing Hélène Landemore's concept of 'democratic reason', she frames extending democracy into the firm as a practical necessity for ethical judgment. She proposes three reforms: first, protecting AI developers by outlawing non-disclosure and non-disparagement clauses that silence staff on safety risks, enacting whistleblower protection, and giving tech workers collective standing over corporate strategy with independent reporting channels and formal representation before model deployment; second, establishing a binding right to co-decision over workplace AI after the Meta case where Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp introduced tools tracking employees' keystrokes, mouse clicks and screen content for training data, requiring prior negotiation of any monitoring system plus collective bargaining on AI deployment, veto rights for works councils or trade unions backed by independent technical experts, and a strict ban on automated firing; third, democratizing boardrooms through worker-elected directors moving toward dual-majority governance where strategic decisions require consent from both capital and labour. Ferreras warns that leaving governance to self-regulation and occasional whistleblowers will entrench an unaccountable algorithmic oligarchy, arguing accountability begins with giving builders of these systems and those they govern an enforceable voice from the code floor to the boardroom.
items.title: AI safety whistleblowers resigning signals broken corporate governance

items.summary: A Singapore court sentenced 44-year-old Christopher Sebastian Bland to two days' jail and a S$3,000 fine (US$2,329) after he slapped a woman's buttocks at a nightclub. The prosecutor called the venue "a significant aggravating factor" and urged deterrence, noting public entertainment outlets were the third most common location for molestation in 2025.
